documented: libpq documents postgres:// and postgresql:// with optional user[:password]@, host/port, database and query parts; credentials have no documented three-character minimum.
Named query parameters may supply hierarchical connection values, including password. Unix socket hosts may be omitted, supplied in query host, or percent-encoded in the authority.

IPv6 authority addresses use brackets; comma-separated host[:port] entries, including empty default hosts and ports, are documented. Query host, hostaddr and port lists have corresponding cardinalities, except one port may apply to all hosts.

The PostgreSQL 18 source frames components before percent decoding, rejects malformed escapes and encoded NUL, preserves literal plus signs, requires exactly one unescaped equals sign per query parameter, and accepts an empty query or a trailing ampersand.
The libpq userinfo lookahead stops at slash but not question mark: a query before any slash must escape a literal at-sign to avoid being parsed as userinfo.

Titus v1.2.9 provides candidate context only: its minimum username/password/host lengths and exclusion of IPv6/query passwords are not libpq grammar and are not inherited. Its per-host-userinfo example is not the documented single-userinfo multihost grammar.
assumptions: These synthetic values assert local recognition of exposed nonempty database passwords, not valid accounts, reachable databases or successful authentication. No network verifier is used.

The detector retains any nonempty authority or password query value as secret evidence even when a later query assignment overrides it. Public addresses, usernames, database names, passfile paths and empty passwords alone are not secrets.

Unknown or future query option names and unrelated option values do not suppress an otherwise exposed password; unlike PQconninfoParse, this scanner does not validate the option vocabulary or complete connection configuration.

URI structural validation uses per-component PathUnescape, not net/url.Parse or ParseQuery: Go's general authority parser does not model libpq multihost/escaped socket authorities and its query parser applies HTML-form plus semantics. Percent decoding is nonrecursive and is never applied to whole input values.

The local structural cap is 16 KiB per complete candidate. Ports are conservatively empty/default or decimal 1-65535; signed or whitespace-padded libpq integer spellings are not inferred from URI port grammar. DNS reachability and hostname ownership are not checked.

Raw non-URI bytes, fragments and malformed suffixes are consumed with the candidate and rejected rather than yielding a valid prefix. Whitespace, double quotes, backticks and angle brackets delimit raw-value candidates; apostrophes are legal component characters and matching single-quote wrappers are stripped contextually. URI-internal whitespace or wrapper characters must be percent-escaped.

Bracketed hosts must parse as IPv6, including percent-escaped zone identifiers; unbracketed hosts follow URI reg-name syntax and can contain escaped socket paths. This is intentionally stricter than libpq accepting some malformed hosts for later resolver failure.
evidence.fixture_method: All inputs are hand-constructed synthetic connection strings using reserved .invalid hosts, documentation IP ranges, local socket paths and invented credentials. Positives distinguish minimal credentials, URI component escaping, libpq query semantics, optional/default hosts and authority/query multihost forms. Negatives cover public/empty-password values, malformed full candidates, libpq-vs-Go parser differences, invalid host-list structure and scheme adjacency; none is copied from a real deployment.
